model_fitness.best_available_model: CDD patient-derived guided cortical organoids with isogenic controls on multielectrode arrays (EVIDENCE PMID:40930428), paired with Cdkl5 KO mouse convulsant-threshold EEG and visual evoked potentials as the in vivo arm (EVIDENCE PMID:24838000).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID:40930428): CDD patient organoid-derived excitatory cortical neurons show increased synchrony and increased weighted mean firing rate on MEA — a measurable network hyperexcitability phenotype in human CDKL5-mutant tissue — alongside reduced phospho-EB2. INFERENCE (supportive): because pEB2 and the firing phenotype coexist in one preparation, target engagement and the therapeutic readout can be dissociated in a single assay.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Forebrain glutamatergic cortical neurons: yes (EVIDENCE PMID:40930428). GABAergic interneurons: only partially, since guided dorsal-forebrain organoids are interneuron-poor; the inhibitory arm needs MGE-patterned co-culture or the mouse, which covers both populations with cell-type-resolved behaviour (EVIDENCE PMID:24838000).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: In vitro: weighted mean firing rate, burst structure, network synchrony; phospho-EB2 and phospho-rpS6. In vivo: convulsant EEG threshold, VEP amplitude, dendritic arborization (EVIDENCE PMID:24838000).
model_fitness.important_limitations: EVIDENCE (contradictory, PMID:40930428): the phenotype is protocol-dependent — NGN2-induced neurons from the same patients showed no MEA or neurite difference despite reduced pEB2, so the assay window is fragile. EVIDENCE (contradictory, PMID:24838000): Cdkl5 KO mice have no spontaneous seizures, so the clinical primary endpoint cannot be modelled, only seizure threshold. INFERENCE: organoid hyperexcitability is early/developmental, lacks mature glia and X-inactivation mosaicism, and may not model established pharmacoresistant epilepsy.

plan.critical_question: Does lowering network excitability by the mechanisms already in CDD trials normalise the CDD-specific network phenotype, or does it suppress firing equally in mutant and isogenic control neurons (generic dampening, not correction)? This distinguishes disease modification from the demonstrated modest-seizure-reduction ceiling.
plan.proposed_experiment: Step 1 (decisive): record CDD organoid neurons vs isogenic controls on MEA across the early window where hyperexcitability is present, testing a concentration-response panel of the clinically precedented CDD mechanisms — ganaxolone (NCT03572933), fenfluramine (NCT03861871, NCT05064878), bexicaserin (NCT05626634), soticlestat (NCT03694275) — plus one Akt/rpS6 probe in each direction (an mTOR inhibitor and an IGF-1/PI3K-activating stimulus) to resolve the unspecified direction of correction. Primary analysis is the genotype x drug interaction on firing rate and synchrony, not the main effect of drug. Measure pEB2 and phospho-rpS6 at endpoint. Run the identical panel in NGN2 neurons from the same donors as a built-in negative control (phenotype absent, PMID:40930428). Step 2 (only for mechanisms with a genotype-selective effect): dose Cdkl5 KO mice over a defined developmental window with convulsant-threshold EEG and VEP amplitude as co-primaries, plus dendritic arborization and cortical phospho-rpS6/pEB2.
plan.model: CDD patient-derived guided cortical organoid neurons vs isogenic controls on MEA (EVIDENCE PMID:40930428), with NGN2-induced neurons from the same donors as a phenotype-null specificity arm; confirmation in Cdkl5 KO mice using convulsant-threshold EEG and VEP (EVIDENCE PMID:24838000).
plan.primary_readout: Genotype x drug interaction term for MEA weighted mean firing rate and network synchrony (mutant values moved toward isogenic control, larger effect in mutant than control). Secondary: phospho-rpS6 normalisation; pEB2 expected unchanged, confirming the agent acts downstream of CDKL5. In vivo: VEP amplitude and convulsant EEG threshold.
plan.supportive_result: At least one mechanism produces significant genotype-selective normalisation — mutant firing/synchrony returns toward control at a concentration leaving control networks largely unaffected — absent in the NGN2 arm, ideally with phospho-rpS6 correction; and in vivo the same agent raises convulsant threshold AND increases VEP amplitude in Cdkl5 KO mice. Interpretation: a CDD-specific excitability node exists and the route may be disease-modifying, not only symptomatic.
plan.negative_result: All agents suppress firing similarly in mutant and control networks (main effect, no interaction), or correct firing in vitro with no VEP improvement in vivo. Interpretation: non-specific excitability dampening, i.e. the already-demonstrated clinical ceiling (INFERENCE contradictory, MONDO:0100039 — seizures are pharmacoresistant by definition; EVIDENCE contradictory, NCT03635073 — soticlestat failed powered Phase 3 in rare epilepsies).
plan.decision_enabled: A genotype-selective hit justifies a focused in vivo package and, for an already-dosed drug, a CDD-specific clinical hypothesis with VEP as a non-seizure pharmacodynamic endpoint. A pure main-effect result retires mechanism-blind repurposing here: redirect spend to identifying the neuron subtype and developmental window that generate the epileptic phenotype and to building a seizure-competent CDD model, rather than funding another Phase 2 signal-seeking study. Either outcome also validates or kills the organoid MEA platform as the field's screening assay.

model_fitness.best_available_model: The same CDD patient-derived cortical organoid MEA / phospho-rpS6 platform (EVIDENCE PMID:40930428), used as a target-discovery tool and not as an efficacy model for a biologic. No model is adequate for a therapeutic biologic claim, because the limiting question is whether a cell-surface node exists at all.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially. EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID:24838000): Akt/rpS6 signalling is measurably altered in Cdkl5 KO mice, so the axis a growth-factor biologic would engage is perturbed. EVIDENCE (inconclusive, PMID:30266824): the causal chain from lost substrate phosphorylation to epilepsy is unestablished, so neither the receptor to bind nor the direction of correction can be nominated. INFERENCE (contradictory): no model can test an agent whose target has not been named.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes for forebrain glutamatergic neurons in vitro (PMID:40930428); but culture bypasses the blood-brain barrier entirely, which is precisely the constraint that decides a biologic's fate. The model is cell-type relevant and delivery-irrelevant.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Phospho-rpS6 and phospho-Akt (pathway engagement), MEA firing rate and synchrony (functional consequence), pEB2 (CDKL5-axis control), neurite morphology.
model_fitness.important_limitations: No in vitro model reports CNS delivery, chronic dosing from infancy, immunogenicity against an endogenous-homologue ligand, or mitogenic risk — the dominant risks here (INFERENCE, contradictory). No spontaneous-seizure model exists (EVIDENCE PMID:24838000), so the clinical endpoint is unreachable for an agent that cannot be cheaply iterated.

plan.critical_question: Is there any cell-surface receptor whose agonism or blockade reproducibly normalises network excitability or Akt/rpS6 signalling in CDD neurons — i.e. does a biologic-accessible node exist at all? Until this is yes, every downstream biologic question (BBB shuttle, format, dosing) is premature.
plan.proposed_experiment: Do not open a biologic program. Run a bounded target-nomination experiment embedded in the small-molecule study above, at marginal extra cost: apply a short panel of recombinant extracellular ligands acting through surface receptors that converge on PI3K/Akt/rpS6 — IGF-1, an IGF-1-derived tripeptide, BDNF (TrkB), and one control growth factor — at two concentrations, within the developmental window in which the hyperexcitability phenotype is present. Primary analysis is the genotype x ligand interaction on phospho-rpS6/phospho-Akt and on MEA firing and synchrony; pEB2 measured as an expected-unchanged control. The biologic is used purely as a pharmacological probe to test whether a surface node exists.
plan.model: CDD patient-derived cortical organoid neurons vs isogenic controls on MEA with phospho-rpS6/phospho-Akt readouts (EVIDENCE PMID:40930428), plus NGN2-derived neurons from the same donors as a phenotype-null specificity arm. Fitness inadequate for efficacy, adequate only for target nomination.
plan.primary_readout: Genotype-selective normalisation of phospho-rpS6/phospho-Akt toward isogenic control values, and whether that normalisation carries through to MEA firing rate and network synchrony.
plan.supportive_result: A ligand corrects phospho-rpS6 AND network firing selectively in mutant neurons, absent in the NGN2 arm. That nominates a candidate surface receptor node; only then is a biologic worth a feasibility assessment, which must start with CNS delivery (BBB-shuttle maturity, intrathecal gradient modelling) before any molecule engineering, and be compared head-to-head with a CNS-penetrant small molecule hitting the same node.
plan.negative_result: No ligand produces a genotype-selective effect, or pathway correction occurs without functional benefit on MEA. Interpretation: no demonstrated biologic-accessible node in CDD, which together with the delivery constraint (INFERENCE contradictory: continuous, uniform, dendrite-level modulation of every forebrain neuron from infancy is the hardest biologic delivery problem; antibodies cross an intact BBB at fractions of a percent of plasma level) closes the modality.
plan.decision_enabled: Pre-registers the only condition under which a CDD biologic program should be opened, and otherwise keeps it closed for the cost of a few extra wells — explicitly avoiding the stated failure mode of years of BBB-shuttle engineering for a target never shown to be right. Landscape evidence supports deprioritisation: the entire retrieved CDD interventional space is small-molecule or dietary with no biologic in development (EVIDENCE contradictory, NCT03572933, NCT03861871, NCT03694275, NCT05626634), consistent with the bottleneck being mechanism rather than modality.
